review: 1:4 לַיְלָה לְבֹקֶר יָבֹא — 'night shall turn to morning'; the Arabic is 'a night, then the day comes', and the Hebrew infinitive-like sequence keeps the 8 syllables.
2:3–2:4 אַל־תָּשִׁיתִי לֵב לַצַּר / רֶגַע הָעֲבֹר — 'do not set your heart on the foe: the crossing is a moment'; the Arabic الْعُبُور ('crossing') is the pilgrimage image, kept as עֲבֹר.

3:2 מִצְוַת דּוֹדִי הַבָּהִיר — 'my Beloved's command, the radiant One'; the Arabic أَمْرُ رَبِّي ذِي الْبَهَاء is a construct with a descriptive apposition, which Hebrew reproduces with the adjective.
4:2 כּוֹכַב־שַׁחַר — 'morning star' (Rev 2:28, 22:16); the Arabic الْعَجِيب ('wondrous') becomes נִפְלָא to keep the line at eight.
5:4 וְלִבִּי בוֹ יִיטַב — 'and my heart shall be glad in Him'; the Arabic يَطِيب is literally 'is good/sweet', and the yiph'il of יטב carries the same double sense.
